sentences.text: Shargaotis is an extinct genus of bird belonging to the family Otididae, commonly known as bustards. The genus contains only one known species, Shargaotis ignipes, which is known from a fragment of a tibiotarsus.
This animal is most similar to the living genera Otis and Chlamydotis.
The genus name Shargaotis combines the type locality 'Sharga' with the name of the great bustard, Otis, while the species name ignipes means 'fiery-footed' or 'extremely fast' in Latin.
Shargaotis fossils were discovered at the Sharga locality in western Mongolia, which contains Miocene-aged rock outcrops.
The fossils were collected during Soviet/Russian-Mongolian Paleontological Expeditions conducted in 1978, 1979, 1984, and 2001.
The holotype specimen is housed at the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences under accession number PIN 4869/249.
Three other bustard bone fragments from the site are known, including a distal left tibiotarsus distinct from Shargaotis and a base phalanx forming the major wing finger.
Shargaotis lived during the Middle Miocene epoch in Mongolia.
Researchers suggest that two additional bustard fragments similar to Chlamydotis might belong to Shargaotis, though they are currently classified as indeterminate.
